So many sloppy “datapoints” being posted here.

If you want to be helpful, you need to provide:

  • How many personal cards of any kind in last 24 months
  • How many chase business cards in last 24 months, and what type (ink, co-brand)
  • Exactly What card did you just get approved/denied for, and on what date.
  • What busniess structure did you apply under (Sole Prop, LLC, S-corp)

N/24 is not a sloppy datapoint. It has a precise meaning:

N/24 = number of CCs <24 months old reporting on the personal bureau pulled, at the time it was pulled.

Business structure is a separate DP that makes n/24 useful in the context of this post.

Date is not a useful DP unless BOTH date of application and date of final denial/approval are included.

The 5/24 rule means you need to be under 5/24.

So yes, the 3/24 rule would mean you need to be under 3/24.

It might be targeted mostly at applications submitted after 9/15 or so, many “approved” DPs were from folks submitted before 9/15 and called recon after that.

IIRC when 5/24 first rolled out there were also lots of confusions and theories on what counts, what cards does it affect and what bypasses it, took more than a year or two for the dust to settle as Chase seemed to believe in “profit by obscurity” and was also actively changing the rules after the roll out.

Regardless it seems safe to draw the following conclusions:

1. Chase has further tightened up their sole prop biz card approval process, including not as willing to move CL from existing biz cards on recon calls now. This means that the decision to tighten up is not purely credit risk driven, more like RAT/anti-churning, esp. given how many sole props are “business” owners. Their recent history points to further tightening down the road.

2. There’s little reason to care about their X/24 rules going forward unless you are just starting out or have a very specific and highly unusual situation. Their current personal card line-up is not very competitive (trying to put it nicely here) and their biz cards’ “expected rewards values” have also dropped below the threshold for serious consideration for many (card gives a SUB worth $2000 + card is expected to be approved with a 10% chance even if you wait till 2/24 = card gives you a expected rewards value of $200, worse than most credit union CCs’ SUBs).
